prompt: Ana runs `docker run postgres:17` on her Windows laptop with Docker Desktop. Where does the `postgres` process run?
hint: Which kernel can run a Linux binary?

choices.text: Directly on Windows, as a Windows process translated by Docker
choices.why: Windows cannot run a Linux binary; Desktop does not translate it.

choices.text: In the Linux VM that Docker Desktop manages
choices.why: Right. The command stays on Windows; the container runs in the VM.

choices.text: On Docker's servers in the cloud
choices.why: Nothing leaves the laptop except the image download.

choices.text: Inside the Docker Desktop window
choices.why: The window only shows lists and settings.

prompt: Bruno installs Docker Desktop on his Linux laptop, which already has Docker Engine. He runs `docker ps` and his old containers are missing. Why?
hint: How many engines does his laptop have now?

choices.text: Desktop deleted them while installing itself
choices.why: Nothing was deleted; they are on the other engine.

choices.text: Linux containers cannot run under Desktop
choices.why: Desktop runs Linux containers, in its own VM.

choices.text: It now talks to Desktop's engine
choices.why: Right: Desktop runs its own VM and engine. Two engines, two sets of containers; `docker context` chooses.

choices.text: He needs to log in to Docker Hub to see them
choices.why: Containers are local; no login lists them.

prompt: On her new Apple silicon Mac, an internal image of Ana's company starts but runs several times slower than on her old Intel Mac. What is the likely cause?
hint: Which processors was the image built for?

choices.text: The image exists only for `amd64`, so it runs under emulation in the `arm64` VM
choices.why: Right. It runs, through Rosetta or QEMU, and slowly.

choices.text: Apple silicon is slower than Intel at everything
choices.why: Native `arm64` images run fast; the issue is the image's architecture.

choices.text: Desktop gives the VM one processor by default
choices.why: The VM's size is a setting, and it would slow every image, not this one.

choices.text: The image's layers are compressed differently on a Mac
choices.why: Layers are the same bytes everywhere; compression is not the issue.

prompt: Match each system to where Docker Desktop runs the Linux kernel.

pairs.right: A VM through Apple's virtualization framework
A VM using KVM, not the host's own kernel

right_distractors: Directly in the host's kernel, with no VM

prompt: A company with 400 employees wants every developer on Docker Desktop. Under the terms the lesson describes, what does it need?
hint: Two thresholds; it passes one of them.

choices.text: Nothing, Docker Desktop is free for any use
choices.why: It is free for small businesses, personal use, education and non-commercial open source.

choices.text: A paid subscription
choices.why: Right: 250 or more employees, or more than 10 million dollars in revenue.

choices.text: A Linux server for each developer
choices.why: That is not a licensing condition; Engine on Linux is simply free.

choices.text: Permission from Microsoft for WSL 2
choices.why: WSL 2 ships with Windows; the condition is Docker's.

prompt: Docker Desktop on a new Windows laptop refuses to start, saying virtualisation is not available. What is the first thing to check?
hint: It is not a Windows setting.

choices.text: Whether the Docker Hub account is verified
choices.why: No account is needed to start the engine.

choices.text: Hardware virtualisation in the firmware
choices.why: Right: Intel VT-x or AMD-V, which some laptops ship with switched off.

choices.text: Whether PostgreSQL is installed
choices.why: Nothing about databases is involved in starting Desktop.

choices.text: Whether the laptop has more than 64 GB of memory
choices.why: A VM does not need that much; the message is about virtualisation itself.

prompt: Ana's laptop has 32 GB of memory. Her database container keeps being killed with exit code 137 under Docker Desktop. What should she check after the container's own limit?
hint: Containers live inside something with its own size.

choices.text: The laptop's swap file
choices.why: The containers never see the laptop's memory, only the VM's.

choices.text: The Docker Hub rate limit
choices.why: Pull limits do not kill running containers.

choices.text: The size the VM was given in the settings
choices.why: Right. Containers cannot use more than the VM has, whatever the laptop has.

choices.text: Whether the image is `amd64` or `arm64`
choices.why: Emulation makes things slow; it does not cause 137.

prompt: Put the Windows installation in order.
items: Switch on hardware virtualisation in the firmware
Run Docker Desktop's installer, keeping the WSL 2 option
Start Docker Desktop and wait for the engine

prompt: Why does the lesson recommend Docker Engine rather than Docker Desktop for most Linux users?
hint: What does Desktop need on Linux that Engine does not?

choices.text: Desktop for Linux has no command line
choices.why: It has the same `docker` command.

choices.text: Engine needs no VM on Linux
choices.why: Right: it uses the host's kernel directly. On Linux there is no kernel to borrow, so the VM is overhead.

choices.text: Engine runs Windows containers too
choices.why: Engine on Linux runs Linux containers only.

choices.text: Desktop for Linux cannot pull from Docker Hub
choices.why: It pulls like any other engine.

prompt: `docker version` prints a `Client` block and then an error instead of a `Server` block. What does that mean?

choices.text: The `docker` command is broken and must be reinstalled
choices.why: The client answered; it is the part that works.

choices.text: The command works, and the engine is not reachable
choices.why: Right. Start the engine, or check which context the client is using.

choices.text: The image cache is full
choices.why: Version does not read images at all.

choices.text: Docker Hub is down
choices.why: `docker version` does not contact a registry.

prompt: On an Apple silicon Mac with Docker Desktop, what do the two `OS/Arch` lines of `docker version` say?

choices.text: Both `darwin/arm64`
choices.why: The server runs in a Linux VM, so it cannot say `darwin`.

choices.text: Both `linux/arm64`
choices.why: The client runs on macOS itself.

choices.text: `darwin/arm64` for the client and `linux/arm64` for the server
choices.why: Right. The disagreement is the VM, printed.

choices.text: `darwin/amd64` for both halves, because both run under Rosetta emulation
choices.why: Neither half is emulated; both are native `arm64`.

prompt: Put the steps `hello-world` describes in order.
items: The daemon pulls the image from Docker Hub
The daemon creates a container that runs the program
The output is streamed back to the client

prompt: Docker Desktop adds a context and makes it current, so the same `docker` command reaches the VM. That context is called ___.
hint: Two words joined by a hyphen.

prompt: On Docker Desktop, `docker info` reports 4 CPUs and about 8 GB of memory on a laptop with 10 cores and 32 GB. Which numbers limit Ana's containers?

choices.text: The laptop's 10 cores and 32 GB
choices.why: Containers run in the VM and never see more than it has.

choices.text: The 4 CPUs and 8 GB, the VM's size
choices.why: Right. Raise them in Desktop's settings if containers need more.

choices.text: Neither, containers have no limit on Desktop
choices.why: They are bounded by the VM, and by any limit set on them.

choices.text: Whichever is smaller per container, chosen at random
choices.why: Nothing is random; the VM's size is the ceiling.

prompt: Right after logging in, Ana types `docker ps` and gets "failed to connect to the docker API at unix://…". Docker Desktop is installed. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Her images were deleted overnight
choices.why: Images are not involved in connecting.

choices.text: The application has not started yet
choices.why: Right. The client is fine; the engine in the VM is not up.

choices.text: The `docker` command needs `sudo` on a Mac
choices.why: Desktop sets up access for the user; the message is about reaching the engine.

choices.text: WSL 2 was uninstalled by an update
choices.why: Possible, but far rarer than an engine that has simply not started.

prompt: Which of these does Docker Desktop include? Choose all that apply.
hint: Five things came in the box.

choices.text: A Linux VM it manages
choices.why: Yes, where the containers run.

choices.text: Docker Engine inside that VM
choices.why: Yes: dockerd, containerd and runc.

choices.text: A Windows kernel for Linux containers
choices.why: Linux containers need a Linux kernel, which is why the VM exists.

choices.text: The `docker` command on your own system
choices.why: Yes, with compose and buildx as plugins.
